name: PermitMesh
audiences: AI-agent platform builders defining software-change authorization boundaries
Maintainers evaluating deterministic policy decisions for agent actions
Security and infrastructure teams testing portable agent-work contracts
problems: Agent identity alone does not define which repository, path, action, budget, or time window is authorized
High-risk agent operations need exact tool, argument, approval, claim, and replay boundaries
Teams need reproducible conformance cases rather than policy claims that cannot be tested

offers.name: PermitMesh policy profile and conformance suite

claims.internalStatement: PermitMesh is a transport-neutral, experimental policy-decision profile for AI agents changing software.
claims.publicWording: Evaluate software-change permissions through a portable, transport-neutral policy profile.

claims.internalStatement: The reference CLI evaluates proposed actions deterministically and fails closed with machine-readable violations.
claims.publicWording: Evaluate proposed agent actions deterministically and receive machine-readable allow or deny reasons.

claims.internalStatement: PermitMesh includes a reproducible adversarial conformance suite covering identity, scope, path, budget, approval, claim, fencing, nonce, and completion-evidence edges.
claims.publicWording: Test policy behavior against a reproducible adversarial conformance suite covering scope, budgets, approvals, replay, and completion evidence.

contentPillars: Software-change permits and exact operation binding
prohibitedClaims: Claims that PermitMesh authenticates agents, sandboxes tools, verifies signatures, or enforces its own decisions
Claims that PermitMesh is an adopted standard, security certification, or production security boundary
Claims of guaranteed prompt-injection prevention, zero false allows, or compatibility not demonstrated by evidence
